narrative.overview: This is the character-select screen of a game the visitor already knows how to read. The roster format is the actual information architecture: Dev is the player, each project is a unit with a portrait, a type, the parts it was built from, and a log. The register is bright and saturated, grounded on a lit arena sky rather than a dark void, with warm panels casting hard unblurred shadows. Everything is built from a 4px pixel unit, which is what keeps a playful world from reading as sloppy.
keyCharacteristics: Lit arena sky, never a dark void
Warm panels with 4px ink outlines and hard, unblurred offset shadows
Every measurement a multiple of the 4px pixel unit
Hand-authored 16×16 sprites, never icon-font glyphs or clipart
Pixel display face over a rounded UI face — labels shout, prose reads
Type badges carry classification as real information, not decoration
Motion settles on a spring; nothing snaps

rules.name: The One Meaning Rule
rules.body: Every signal colour carries exactly one meaning: gold is action and achievement, magenta/cyan/green are the three types, live green is API-sourced data.

rules.name: The Live Value Rule
rules.body: Live Green appears only on a value fetched this session. When the API is unavailable the slot reads NO DATA in Ink Soft. There is deliberately no hardcoded fallback.

rules.name: The Daylight Rule
rules.body: The ground stays a lit sky. Near-black grounds, neon-on-black, and CRT glow are permanently out.

rules.name: The Small Text Off Sky Rule
rules.body: White on Arena Sky measures 4.49:1 — large display type only. Any text below 24px must sit on a panel.

rules.name: The Prose Reads Rule
rules.body: Silkscreen never sets a sentence. Anything longer than four words is Baloo 2.

rules.name: The No Blur Rule
rules.body: Every shadow has zero blur radius and zero spread. A blurred shadow instantly reads as a generic web card.

rules.name: The Shadow Is The Ground Rule
rules.body: Panel shadows are always Sky Far, so panels look lit by the same scene.

rules.name: The Authored Sprite Rule
rules.body: Every pictorial element is a hand-authored pixel grid. No icon fonts, no clipart.

dos: Do keep every dimension a multiple of the 4px pixel unit.
Do author new sprites by hand as pixel grids in src/data/sprites.ts.
Do use hard, zero-blur shadows in Sky Far for every raised surface.
Do show inapplicable type badges greyed rather than hiding them — absence is information.
Do set all prose in Baloo 2 and all labels in Silkscreen.
Do render NO DATA in Ink Soft whenever the API has not supplied a value.
Do put small text on a panel, never directly on the sky.
donts: Don't use border-radius, blurred shadows, or gradients on any component surface.
Don't set a sentence in Silkscreen.
Don't add CRT scanlines, screen curvature, glow, or any other retro-arcade costume.
Don't go dark-mode-with-neon. The ground is a lit sky.
Don't reuse a signal colour for a second meaning.
Don't substitute an icon font or clipart where a sprite belongs.
Don't invent a live value when the API is unavailable.
